title: Client Revival Playbook — Escalation Canvas & Rapid Renewal Assessment
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, field-friendly "client revival" playbook designed for quick triage during QBRs and pre-renewal windows. Focus: 30–72 hour assessment to determine whether a customer falls into (A) low-risk monitoring, (B) near-term remediation + standard save plays, or (C) executive escalation and targeted rescue.

How to use this doc (one-pager workflow):
1) Intake (first 30 mins): CSM runs the Renewal Signal Checklist (section A). Fill the top-row of the canvas.
2) Rapid evidence collection (next 2–8 hours): gather metrics, recent incident summaries, usage trends, and top support threads. Attach snippets to the ticket.
3) Triage call (within 24 hours): 20–30m sync between CSM and AE + Solutions SE. Decide path: Monitor / Remediate / Escalate.
4) Execution (24–72 hours): trigger play sequences defined below; if Escalate, notify Exec sponsor and Ops SLA stakeholders.

SECTION A — Renewal Signal Checklist (yes/no/unknown)
- Contract renewal within 90 days: YES/NO
- Monthly usage < 50% of committed: YES/NO
- >2 P1/P2 incidents in last 90 days: YES/NO
- Open unresolved support ticket >14 days: YES/NO
- Product ROI metric declining (engagement, embeddings volume, inference per user): YES/NO
- Exec stakeholder churn risk observed (reorg, budget cuts): YES/NO
- Competing vendor POC underway: YES/NO
- Payment/PO issues flagged: YES/NO

Quick score guide: 0–2 "green" (monitor); 3–4 "amber" (remediate); 5+ "red" (escalate). Use as input, not final decision.

SECTION B — Evidence matrix (fields to paste into ticket)
- Top 3 usage metrics (last 90d): "tokens/day", "active seats using API", "avg latency P50/P95"
- Support trail highlights (last 30d): short bullet for each case (ID, symptom, owner, status)
- Recent change log: any feature regressions, breaking infra changes, config changes (who, when)
- Business signal: contract value, renewal date, expansion opportunities previously discussed

SECTION C — Standard Remediation Plays (Amber bucket)
Objective: restore confidence and show measurable improvement within 14–30 days. Pick 1–2 plays, assign owners, set OKR-style success criteria.
Remediation play #1 — Tactical performance sprint
- Owner: Solutions SE (SSE) + Infra SRE support
- Actions: short tracing session with customer (2h), apply KV-cache tuning or batching config recommended by Optimize team, follow-up perf run within 72h
- Success criteria: P95 latency improved by >=25% OR throughput increased to meet committed usage
- Template email to AE/CSM to request access and schedule: [inline sample included in appendix]

Remediation play #2 — Usage enablement and product adoption push
- Owner: CSM + Customer Education
- Actions: 1-hour enablement workshop for top 3 internal teams, provide quickstart prompts library, 14-day adoption checklist for customer engineering leads
- Success criteria: active integrations doubled OR key adoption metric up by 30% within 30 days

Remediation play #3 — Financial/contract adjustment (short-term retention)
- Owner: AE + RevOps + CSM
- Actions: propose 3-month extension with usage-based credits, or temporary tier bump; record decision in ticket and legal loop
- Success criteria: formal commitment to renewal AND at least one expansion milestone agreed in writing

SECTION D — Executive Escalation (Red bucket)
Escalate when: score triggers red OR customer explicitly signals likely churn OR major contractual/commercial concern.
Escalation steps (timeline 0–72 hours):
- Hour 0–6: CSM files "Executive Escalation" ticket, populates Evidence matrix, pings CRO/Head of CS with 1-paragraph brief + ask (sample brief below).
- Hour 6–24: Executive sync (CRO, Head of CS, AE, CSM, SSE, Head of Product as needed). Prepare one-slide situation brief: problem, impact, options, recommended ask (discount? credits? product dev effort?), cost of inaction.
- Hour 24–72: Execute chosen rescue play (see play list). Provide daily update to execs until renewal decision.

Escalation play examples (pick based on cause):
- Tactical SLA Commitment + Ops Support: allocate dedicated support rotation for 30 days, guaranteed response SLA for P0/P1, include SRE war-room sessions.
- Product Remediation Fast-track: product team triages bug with priority fix and customer validation build within 2–4 weeks.
- Commercial Rescue: structured credits + tie to short extension + clear roadmap milestones; AE presents revised contract and timeline.
- VIP Adoption Partnership: dedicated Solutions Architect, quarterly exec QBR with roadmap commitments, co-marketing offer for joint success story (if appropriate)

SECTION E — Communication templates (short)
- 1-paragraph Exec Brief (CS -> CRO)
Subject: Exec escalation request — [Customer] renewal risk
Hi [Name], we are initiating an executive escalation for [Customer]. Renewal date: [date]. Summary: customer has had X incidents, usage has fallen Y%, and a competing POC is live. Ask: approve 30-day tactical SLA + $XXk credit to bridge to renewal OR approve product team engagement. Attached: Evidence matrix.

- Customer-facing remediation kickoff (CSM -> Customer)
Hi [Customer Admin], thanks for the sync today. We are initiating a short remediation plan focused on [performance/adoption/billing]. Next steps: 1) schedule enablement session (owner: CSM), 2) infra tuning window with SSE (owner: SSE) within 72h, 3) weekly check-ins for 30 days. Expected outcome: restore baseline usage and confirm path to renewal.

SECTION F — Roles & RACI (one-line)
- CSM: single-threaded owner for customer comms, tracks evidence, drives adoption plays
- AE: commercial owner, negotiates credits/contract changes
- SSE: technical lead for remedial actions and performance validation
- SRE/Infra: supports on war-room and escalated performance fixes
- Product PM: triages product defects and scopes fast-track items
- Exec Sponsor (CRO/Head of CS): final decision maker for commercial trade-offs and strategic rescues

SECTION G — Metrics to show in QBR after play execution (minimum required)
- Usage vs committed (tokens/day or inference units) — trend chart last 90 days
- Latency P50/P95 baseline vs post-tuning
- Open case backlog and resolution time trend (30d)
- Adoption indicators (active teams, API keys with >Y calls/day)
- Financial: ARR at risk, credits applied, revised renewal date

SECTION H — Appendix: quick templates and checklist (pasteable)
- Ticket summary headline: "ExecEscalation: [Customer] — renewal [date] — score [X]"
- 24-hour pack format (one paragraph each): Current state; Evidence bullets; Recommended 2 options (cost/time); Ask (what you need from execs)
- Sample success metric line: "By DD/MM expected: increase inference throughput by 40% and reduce P95 from 1.2s to <=0.6s; retain $XXX ARR"

Open questions / notes to iterate:
- Should we require AE sign-off for any commercial credit > $XXk? (needs policy from RevOps)
- Consider a dedicated "rapid remediation" budget for mid-market accounts under $250k ARR — reduces friction for short-term credits
- Integrate a short form into Salesforce so renewal risk flags automatically create the initial ticket

Next steps for this draft:
- CSM team to pilot with 3 flagged accounts during the next renewal wave (Dec-Jan), capture time-to-resolution and outcome
- RevOps to propose an approval threshold matrix for credits within 7 business days
- Product to outline typical fast-track SLAs and feasible timelines for bug fixes

Contact + versioning:
- Owner: Elena Park (elena.park@redwood.com) — please update this doc with pilot learnings.
- Version: 0.3 (internal draft)

Appendix: sample short email snippets (paste-ready)
- Customer ask to schedule enablement:
"Hi [Name], can you do a 60-minute enablement on [date options]? We'll cover 3 integration patterns that remove the most friction we've seen. Please invite your engineering lead."

- Exec ping (Slack):
"@CRO urgent: initiating ExecEscalation for [Customer]. Renewal in 45 days. Summary posted to ticket CS-4823. Request: quick sync today or approval for tactical SLA/credit option."

----
Notes: keep this doc intentionally short and actionable; it's a playbook, not a post-mortem. The next doc will be a more formalized "renewal-tracking workbook" with embedded SFDC queries and a dashboard spec.
